title: Strategy: Newton's inequality as a sum of squares
content: The docstring frames the target: the next Maclaurin/Newton rung after the base step $S_1^2 \ge S_2$, namely $S_2^2 \ge S_1 S_3$ (log-concavity of the elementary symmetric means), resolved for $n = 3$. Unlike the base rung — which collapses to Cauchy-Schwarz — this rung rests on an explicit sum-of-squares certificate $e_2^2 - 3e_1 e_3 = \tfrac12[(ab-bc)^2 + (bc-ca)^2 + (ca-ab)^2]$. Because the certificate is sign-agnostic, the inequality holds for ALL reals, not just nonnegative ones. The general-$n$ cleared form $2(n-2)e_2^2 \ge 3(n-1)e_1 e_3$ is documented; its proof needs Rolle's theorem and is left as the forward open question. NOTE: the general-n, all-k Newton log-concavity is already formalized for NONNEGATIVE reals in AmgmInequalityOQ02OQ02.lean (elemSymm_log_concave, newton_log_concavity_proved). This entry is complementary: at n=3 it drops the nonnegativity hypothesis (sign-agnostic), exhibits the explicit SOS witness, and characterizes equality.

title: The three elementary symmetric polynomials e₁, e₂, e₃
content: Over reals $a, b, c$ the file defines the three elementary symmetric polynomials directly: $e_1 = a+b+c$, $e_2 = ab+bc+ca$, $e_3 = abc$. Working with concrete three-variable polynomials (rather than a Finset-indexed family) is exactly what lets the inequality be discharged by `ring` and `nlinarith` — the whole proof stays inside decidable real-closed-field arithmetic.

title: The sum-of-squares certificate (the engine)
content: `newton_sos_identity` is the heart of the entry: it is the pure ring identity $e_2^2 - 3e_1 e_3 = \tfrac12[(ab-bc)^2 + (bc-ca)^2 + (ca-ab)^2]$. After `simp only [e1, e2, e3]` unfolds the definitions, `ring` verifies the polynomial equality. This exposes the Newton defect as literally half a sum of three squares — the algebraic reason the inequality is true, and simultaneously the reason equality forces $ab = bc = ca$.

title: Cleared form e₂² ≥ 3e₁e₃ for all reals
content: `newton_cleared` reads the inequality straight off the certificate: since the right-hand side of `newton_sos_identity` is a sum of three squares (each `sq_nonneg`), `nlinarith` — fed the identity plus the three `sq_nonneg` facts — closes $e_2^2 \ge 3e_1 e_3$. Crucially there is no hypothesis on the signs of $a, b, c$: Newton's inequality is sign-agnostic, in contrast to Maclaurin's chain which needs nonnegativity to extract real roots at higher rungs.

title: Averaged form S₂² ≥ S₁S₃
content: `newton_base_step` lifts the cleared inequality to the symmetric-means statement $S_2^2 \ge S_1 S_3$ with $S_1 = e_1/3$, $S_2 = e_2/3$, $S_3 = e_3/1$. The averaged defect $(e_2/3)^2 - (e_1/3)(e_3/1)$ equals $(e_2^2 - 3e_1 e_3)/9$ by `ring`; the numerator is $\ge 0$ by `newton_cleared` and the denominator $9 > 0$, so `div_nonneg` and `linarith` finish. Because the denominators $\binom{3}{k}$ are constants, no positivity side-conditions on the variables are needed.

title: The equality locus: ab = bc = ca
content: Two theorems pin down when $S_2^2 = S_1 S_3$. `newton_eq_of_all_eq` shows $a = b = c$ forces equality (a direct `ring` computation after substitution). `newton_products_eq_of_eq` proves the converse content: if equality holds, the sum of squares in the certificate must vanish, so each square is zero (via `sq_nonneg` bounding and `linarith`), and `pow_eq_zero_iff` extracts $ab = bc$ and $bc = ca$. Together they characterize the extremal configuration — the products $ab, bc, ca$ all coincide, i.e. $a = b = c$ for nonzero variables.
